text: Hi Doctor finally I have somewhat of an explanation as to what happened to me on GLP-1. I was taking it for 2 months and not only was I severely constipated (but didn't know it until my hospitalization) because I was still having bowel movements, but suddenly one day I felt nauseas and sick all night finally started vomiting in the morning the next day but the vomit was all fluids, bile, and eventually coffee grounds. I threw up like 5 times all liquid. Then I suddenly had a feeling of unquenchable thirst and everytime I tried to drink any water I would throw it back up. I also had all night pain and cramping from my waist down through my legs. After the dying of thirst feeling and inability to even sip water I called an ambulance (I live alone). Long story short still thirsty after 5 IVs (Im not diabetic), and also I take Suboxone so they did an abdominal xray right after I pooped in the E/R bathroom and the doctor said I was severely and dangerously impacted even though I pooped. She couldn't believe I had gone BEFORE the xrays. Well I had an anion gap and my blood PH was only 7.1 I had metabolic acidosis, lots of ketones/ketosis, then my blood pressure was really low, and I landed in the ICU. They gave me a nasty magnesium citrate drink and other laxatives and I basically 💩 my brains out multiple times. So my question is did I go into ketosis and metabolic acidosis because I was so constipated? Because I was eating food I wasnt starving myself but once I had the nausea I couldn't eat all day of course. By the time I was vomiting no food was in my stomach but I had eaten the day before so what exactly caused that ketosis and subsequent acidosis?  I cant take GLP-1 because between that and the suboxone the constipation gets so severe. Recently I landed in the hospital vomiting fluids non stop and unable to keep water down yet this time I did not have the ketosis or acidosis only the severe fecal impaction again. And I have no idea I'm impacted until they do an x-ray and tell me. Any feedback would be appreciated.

text:
Also pro tip. Take the TDEE estimate of sedentary. Do a very small deficit over about a month or stay at that maintenance. Weigh yourself fasted for 24h for each on the same day of your cycle. This will give you an accurate representation of your ACTUAL weight loss from that deficit.
You can then reverse calculate your ACTUAL TDEE.

(Pounds lost × 3500, ÷4, ÷7. Thats your deficit per day. Calories you averaged + this number is your actual average TDEE)

I was going off a TDEE of 2000 kcal. My actual TDEE is 2600kcal, as a low estimate. I felt like I was LITERALLY DYING on 1400-1600kcal and beat myself up because I was like "it's only 400-600kcal, why is this so hard! Im doing everything right!" and couldn't sustain it. No girlie pop, I was in a deficit of 1000-1200kcal. Like literally the top end of the range of safe weight loss deficit. I would get frustrated some days and eat upto to like 2400kcal & push even harder because I though I ate over maintenance. These calculators don't take into account real life. I have ADHD; my brain doesn't turn off and I'm constantly pacing, fidgeting, getting up and down, running bc I'm late for my bus or class, and I take medications that increase my energy expenditure. It's not exercise (although I do that too 1-2x per week) but it adds up in NEAT.

text:
I started working out and intuitive eating in February 2024 and now it’s August 2025 and I’ve lost 69.8 lbs 
That is FAST weight loss, but I lost about 30 lbs in the first 6 months and then weightloss slowed month by month after that to now about 1 lb/month last month. 
I’ve only done 20 minute strength training workouts. I’ve done 0 HIIT, 0 killer cardio, none of that. 3-5 days/week 20 minute strength training in my living room with dumbells and then walking about 5000-9000 steps/day. 

Eating what my body wants by learning to listen to my hunger. 

So far today I’ve had normal oatmeal with blueberries, hemp seeds, a little brown sugar, and cinnamon. A protein bar, probably like 3/4 of a slice of pumpkin bread idk I was just munchin, some honey almonds, a few m&ms, and some cottage cheese. 
For dinner I’ll probably do leftover cheeseburgers (yes with a bun and normal cheese) and corn on the cob and usually if I get peckish after I’ll have some fruit or chips or popcorn or whatever really. 

When you LISTEN to your body, anything is possible. That means some days I sit the workout out. Some days I don’t get to 5k steps. Some days I am super hungry and eat more than I usually do. Some days I don’t feel well and eat a little less than I usually do. I don’t count calories or macros but I do try to be mindful of protein to just get in about 55-60 grams/day and shove some vitamins from whole food options up in me. 

And yes I’ve worked with an eating disorder specialized registered dietician from April 2024-present because my history will anorexia will tell me to eat as little as humanly possible and that will lead to death. So in interest of not dying and just maintaining a weight I feel comfortable at and trying to gain some muscle so I can support my joint and bone health, I talk to a registered dietician who understands my history.

text:
Great info - thx so much!!🥰 

Im 58 post menopausal and been Keto/paleo consistently for 3 years now.  Seen big improvements in reduction of autoimmune symptoms, severe gut/digestive problems, brain fog, and chronic joint pain I’d delt w/ for decades. 🥳

Main foods are sheep milk yogurt, raw milk kefir (though sadly raw milk is now unavailable in my area of CA 😢) pecorino romano, manchego, raw goat milk cheddar, pastured eggs, grassfed ground beef or lamb, sardines, macadamia, avocados. Also have 1 TBS of grassfed butter, MCT and honey in my am coffee. Eat  1/4-1/2 cup sauerkraut or other fermented veggies with every meal. 

This way of eating has kept me at ideal bodyweight w/ no cravings. Eat 2 meals/day and fast some but not strict w/ it.   I exercise daily with combo of HIT, walking and resistance training. 

Labs have gotten much better too  w/ Triglycerides around 60, HDL 125, A1C 5.3 (still want to get that down!) excellent vitamin D and B12. Crp is 0. Only negative labs are HDL has now gone up (214) and lipo-b is a tad over normal.

Now working on improving metabolic health and getting more deep/REM sleep.  My waking body temps are about 96, and I feel too cold a lot of the time.  I struggle in eating enough calories and not able to eat very big meals when I do eat.  Makes me wonder if I should increase the carbs?? 

Maybe you’ll do a video on improving metabolic health especially for us post menopausal women? 

I will try some of your recommended supplements and thanks so much for always putting out such helpful content! I really appreciate your work! 
🥰🙏
